ender3.notes: PTFE-lined hotend by default - exceeding 240C risks toxic fumes. 250C is Creality's own published figure (product FAQ, 'Ender-3 3D Printer Basic Parameters': highest nozzle temperature 250 degrees Celsius); the firmware would accept 260. e3d_revo_cr_reflashed.display_name: Creality Ender 3 / Pro + E3D Revo CR (firmware reflashed)
e3d_revo_cr_reflashed.description: PTFE-lined stock hotend replaced with an E3D Revo CR AND the firmware reflashed to allow the higher target. Both are required; the part alone does not raise what the machine will accept.
requires: FIRMWARE MUST BE REFLASHED FIRST, to HEATER_0_MAXTEMP >= 315. The part's own documentation says no firmware change is needed - that is true for FITTING it at stock temperatures, and it does NOT make 300C reachable. Creality's stock firmware caps the settable target well below 300, so without the reflash this machine will fault mid-print. Do the reflash, or do not select this variant.

An E3D Revo CR is actually fitted. This ceiling belongs to that specific part - its heater, thermistor, heat break and nozzle are rated together as one assembly - and is not transferable to any other all-metal hotend.
The Revo core matches this machine's 24V supply (Creality's own bill of materials specifies a 24V 40W heater).
e3d_revo_cr_reflashed.notes: 300 C is the last calibrated row in Creality's Marlin thermistor table, so there is no calibrated margin above it - readings past 300 are a linear extrapolation off a nonlinear NTC curve.

HARDWARE FIRST, FIRMWARE SECOND. Creality's own instruction says to flash Ender-3 S1 Pro firmware with no stated ordering; flashing before fitting the titanium throat leaves 305 C settable on a PTFE-lined heat break, which is the exact melt this ceiling exists to prevent.
Reflashed to Ender-3 S1 Pro firmware. Stock S1 firmware is HEATER_0_MAXTEMP 275 with HOTEND_OVERSHOOT 15, capping the machine at 260 C however good the hardware is.
creality_high_temp_block.notes: Creality's wording is 'supports the high temperature printing under 300', and above 300C the silicone sock has to come off. Treat 300 as a boundary, not a midpoint.

_meta.description: Per-printer safety profiles for Kiln G-code validation. The 'default' profile applies when no printer-specific profile matches.

field_semantics.max_hotend_temp: THE MACHINE'S RATED CAPABILITY in C, mirrored from printer_intelligence.json (the manufacturer-spec registry). It is enforced as a CRITICAL block rule by the G-code interceptor. It is NOT a guard band: do not hand-type a margin into it. A value above the rating grants rope the machine was never rated for; a value below it silently caps hardware the owner paid for. Both directions are caught by test_registry_mirror.py, which runs in public CI because both files it compares are public.
field_semantics.max_bed_temp: Same contract as max_hotend_temp, for the heated bed.
field_semantics.policy_margin: Safety MARGIN lives separately and is named: _PTFE_SAFE_MAX (240C) in server.py clamps PTFE-lined hotends below their rating, because the liner degrades before the machine does. That is what a guard band should look like — one named constant derived from a material fact, not a per-printer round number. Add new margins the same way.
field_semantics.why_this_exists: Until 2026-07-20 this file and the registry disagreed on 17 values. printer_intelligence had been backfilled from manufacturer specs; this file never had an equivalent pass, so it had collapsed 250/260/290-rated machines into a round 300. Nothing compared them.
field_semantics.variants: OPTIONAL per-profile map of curated HARDWARE VARIANTS: {variant_id: {field: value}}. The base profile describes the printer AS SHIPPED. A variant describes the same printer after a documented, named hardware change, and restates ONLY the fields that change - everything else is inherited. This is the one place a limit may be HIGHER than the base. A variant is SELECTED by the operator (select_printer_variant); the number always comes from here. There is no code path from a user-supplied value into a variant.
field_semantics.variant_requires: A variant's `requires` list is the set of preconditions that make its ceiling true - a specific named part, a firmware reflash, an install ordering, a supply voltage. Selecting the variant IS the operator's attestation that these are met; Kiln cannot verify them remotely. When a part's own documentation would lead an operator to believe a precondition is unnecessary, state the precondition FIRST and name it in the variant id, so satisfying the documentation cannot be mistaken for satisfying the requirement. Where a precondition cannot be made explicit, ship NO variant.
field_semantics.variant_sourcing: Sourcing for these numbers is NOT in this file and must not be added to it - no urls, no source fields, and no prose about which vendors publish what. Each variant traces to a manufacturer primary source recorded privately; that record is the research, and the research does not ship. What ships here is the enforced value plus the preconditions an operator must have met, because both are needed to print safely. Sourcing metadata appearing in this file is a leak, not documentation.
field_semantics.two_published_answers: WHEN A MANUFACTURER PUBLISHES TWO DIFFERENT NUMBERS FOR ONE MACHINE, TAKE THE LOWER. Decided 2026-08-07. A vendor's manual and its firmware routinely disagree: the manual states what they rate the machine at, the firmware states what it will actually accept, and neither is wrong. This file used to answer that two ways - max_hotend_temp is described as the RATED CAPABILITY, while prusa_mk4 carries a comment saying the ceiling 'tracks achievable capability, not marketing'. Both readings gave the same answer on the mk4 (spec 300, firmware 290 -> 290) so the contradiction went unnoticed until ender3_v2, where the manual says 250 and the firmware allows 260. Lower-of-the-two reproduces the mk4 result and is the only reading conservative in both directions. Record BOTH figures in the notes so the next reader can see it was a choice.

_meta.variant_bucketing_rule: IF SHARED OR AGGREGATED PRINTER INTELLIGENCE IS EVER BUILT ON TOP OF THIS DATA, READ THIS FIRST. A curated profile describes a printer as shipped; a variant describes one person's modified machine. They are different objects and must never merge into one number. (1) Any shared or aggregated printer intelligence keys on (model, variant), NEVER model alone. (2) A machine whose variant is UNDECLARED contributes to NOTHING - not to the base bucket, not to a catch-all. Undeclared is not a synonym for stock. (3) The (model, variant) bucket must exist before any data is written into it; do not create it by first write. A tweaked printer feeding the base model's pool would silently teach every stock owner of that model a number their hardware cannot survive. Existing federation rails already carry the cohort-key discipline this extends - see canonical_printer_model() in kiln/community_outbox.py.

bambu_h2s.notes: Enclosed CoreXY, direct drive. All-metal hardened-steel factory hotend (abrasive-ready out of the box). Active heated chamber to 65C (engages ~40C) with a 120C bed and 350C hotend - the full engineering-material envelope (ABS/ASA/PC/PA/CF). AMS 2 Pro multi-material via the AMS Hub. 1000 mm/s toolhead = feedrate 60000. Volumetric-flow ceiling 32 mm3/s is conservative pending field data on the high-flow hotend. AI chamber monitoring + physical clump detector; no LiDAR first-layer inspection.

voron_0.notes: Compact enclosed CoreXY kit. 270C IS NOT A HOTEND RATING. It is the max_temp this machine's own designer ships in every current config for it, sitting above a sensor_type line left blank for the builder to fill in - an unconfigured default rather than a measurement of anything. No hotend ceiling is published for this machine, and that is a real absence rather than a gap in the research: it is a kit, the hotend is not the kit maker's product, so there is no number for them to state. The honest way up is to select the variant matching the hotend actually fitted. NOT EVERY HOTEND THIS MACHINE ACCEPTS HAS ONE. Voron publish mounts for around ten, and only the one below could be given a ceiling; Dragon and Dragonfly builds in particular have no variant, because those parts ship no heater and no thermistor and their maker states no operating temperature, so there is nothing to enforce and Kiln will not invent a figure to fill the space. A blocked print here means Kiln does not know your hotend, not that your hotend is unsafe.

e3d_revo_voron.description: An E3D Revo Voron on the toolhead mount Voron publish for it - the Mini Afterburner on the V0.1, the hotend mount on the V0.2. The ceiling belongs to that assembly - heater, thermistor, heat break and nozzle rated together as one part - and not to the machine.
requires: An E3D Revo Voron is actually fitted. This ceiling is not transferable to another hotend, and not to another Revo either: the Revo range is several different parts with different ratings, and only this one was checked against this machine.

CHECK THE CORE VOLTAGE AGAINST YOUR PSU. Revo cores are sold in 12V and 24V and the part alone does not tell you which you have. This is a kit whose builder chooses the power supply, so there is no printer-to-voltage lookup to fall back on - read it off the machine. A 12V cartridge on a 24V rail dissipates roughly four times its rating.

printer.cfg declares the matching sensor_type AND a max_temp at or above what you intend to print. This machine ships with sensor_type commented out and max_temp 270, so until the builder fills in both, its own firmware aborts the print above 270 no matter what Kiln permits.
e3d_revo_voron.notes: 300C is the part maker's figure for the complete assembly. A nozzle change can impose its own LOWER limit that this field cannot express - a hardened steel nozzle in an aluminium block is not suitable above 240C - and selecting this variant does not lift that.

voron_2.notes: Full-size enclosed CoreXY kit. 270C IS NOT A HOTEND RATING. It is the max_temp this machine's own designer ships above a sensor_type line left blank for the builder to fill in - an unconfigured default rather than a measurement of anything. No hotend ceiling is published for this machine, because it is a kit and the hotend is not the kit maker's product. Select the variant matching the hotend you fitted. NOT EVERY COMMON HOTEND HAS ONE: Dragon and Rapido builds have no variant, because those parts ship no heater and no thermistor and their maker states no operating temperature, so there is nothing to enforce and Kiln will not invent a figure to fill the space. A blocked print here means Kiln does not know your hotend, not that your hotend is unsafe. That is also why PA-CF is out of reach at this base: Kiln's suggested 275C for it sits above 270, and on an as-shipped config it is unreachable anyway, since the machine's own firmware stops first. Declare the hotend and it becomes reachable. SOME COMMON BUILDS BELONG BELOW 270 AND YOU MUST SET THAT YOURSELF: an E3D V6 with its silicone sock fitted, which is how a V6 is normally assembled, is rated 260C by its maker - under this base. No variant can express that, because a variant may only raise a ceiling and never lower one; set the lower figure as max_temp in your own printer.cfg, which is the backstop that actually stops the heater.

ratrig_vcore3.notes: CoreXY kit. The hotend ceiling is a property of the hotend the builder fitted, not of the machine, so 285C here is the as-built default: it is what RatRig's own firmware ships for every NTC-sensor hotend they support, including the one they name as standard. A PT1000-sensor hotend is rated higher - select that variant rather than overriding this number. Usually EVA toolhead.

pt1000_hotend.description: A hotend using a PT1000 sensor rather than the NTC thermistor most V-Core 3 builds ship with. The ceiling tracks the SENSOR, not the hotend brand, metal or flow class. Covers Rapido Plus, Rapido Plus UHF and Goliath.
requires: The fitted hotend genuinely uses a PT1000 sensor. An NTC hotend is 285 C in RatRig's own configuration whatever its brand, flow class or block metal.
Klipper printer.cfg declares the matching sensor_type. A PT1000 read as an NTC misreports temperature outright.
pt1000_hotend.notes: This does not lift a separate, LOWER limit: a hardened steel nozzle in an aluminium block is not suitable above 240C. That is a nozzle/block pairing limit and no machine or hotend field can express it.

AON3D ships a Klipper-based firmware on current machines (units at or below application version v2022.07.04.21.14 run Marlin) behind AON3D's own browser interface. qidi_plus4.notes: Enclosed CoreXY with a 370 C bimetal nozzle and 65 C independent chamber heating — the highest hotend of any consumer machine here, and enough for unfilled PPS. Klipper firmware with a Fluidd web interface, so the existing Moonraker adapter reaches it.

qidi_q1_pro.notes: Compact enclosed CoreXY, 350 C ceramic-heated bimetal hotend with 60 C independent chamber heating. Klipper firmware — reachable through the existing Moonraker adapter.

qidi_x_max3.notes: Large-format enclosed CoreXY, 350 C hotend, 65 C actively heated chamber, integrated dryer box. Ships both a copper-alloy and a hardened-steel hotend, so abrasive filled grades need no upgrade. Klipper firmware — existing Moonraker adapter reaches it.

qidi_q2.notes: Enclosed CoreXY with a 370 C bimetal hardened-steel nozzle and 65 C second-generation independent chamber heating — the same hotend ceiling as the Plus 4 in a smaller frame, so unfilled PPS is in range. Klipper, so the existing Moonraker adapter reaches it.

ender3_s1_pro.notes: Sprite Pro full-metal direct-drive extruder, rated 300C against 260C for the base S1. Bed is 100C per Creality's spec table - a distributor listing says 110, and the manufacturer's own figure is the one enforced here. Creality describes the hot end as 'full metal' and does not state that the hot zone is PTFE-free, so do not assume it. Open-frame bed-slinger, so ABS and ASA still warp without an enclosure.

aon_hylo.notes: Industrial high-temperature FFF. Dual independent extruders, actively heated 250 C chamber, 250 C bed, 500 C nozzle — enough to hold ULTEM 9085/1010 and PPSU at the chamber temperature their properties depend on, which the AON-M2+ cannot. Ships HEPA/activated-carbon emission filtration; even so, these polymers decompose into hazardous products and the chamber runs far above skin-burn temperature, so let it cool before opening and keep room ventilation independent of the filter. Needs 208-240VAC 50A single phase and 75-135 psig compressed air for the vacuum chuck. Kiln does not control this printer: USB is file upload only and management is through AON3D's cloud, so there is no third-party control path — Kiln advises, it does not drive.

intamsys_610ht.notes: Industrial high-temperature FFF. Dual nozzles, actively heated 300 C chamber, 300 C platform, 500 C extruder — the widest thermal envelope in the registry, clearing ULTEM 9085/1010 and PPSU with margin. INTAMSYS publishes NO onboard fume filtration for this model; their own safety data sheets for ULTEM and PPSU require exhaust ventilation where the material is molten, so facility extraction is the operator's responsibility here, not the machine's. Front and top doors carry electromagnetic safety locks driven by an independent safety PLC, with a chamber temperature sensor and a separate temperature limiter as redundant sensing, designed against EN60204. Treat the interlocks as load-bearing: a 300 C chamber is a burn hazard consumer printers do not have. Kiln does not control this printer: INTAMSYS markets an SDK but publishes no API, so there is no verified third-party control path — Kiln advises, it does not drive.

visionminer_22idex_v4.notes: Industrial IDEX with a 500 C hotend and 200 C bed but only a 100 C actively heated chamber. Vision Miner's sales list names PEEK, PEKK, ULTEM 9085/1010 and PPSU; their own temperature guide is more careful, capping the chamber at 100 C for every one of them and telling you to verify each material's real requirement. Kiln does that verification: the hotend and bed clear these polymers, the chamber does not, so they are refused here. Everything up to PPS, PC and PA-CF runs comfortably at the vendor's 30-200 mm/s high-temperature range. Hold the documented 15-minute heat soak before starting, and never pre-heat the nozzle during it. Ships built-in HEPA and activated-carbon filtration with an optional external fume-extraction port. Runs RepRapFirmware on a Duet 3 with Duet Web Control and accepts standard RepRap G-code, so it slices in PrusaSlicer or OrcaSlicer today, and Kiln drives it over that same HTTP interface — register it with type 'duet'. That control path has not yet been exercised against this machine in person, so treat the first job on it as a supervised one.
